intro.title: Not Many Fathers

verses.text: Even if you had ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.

body.t: Paul names the church's problem in one sentence: **ten thousand guardians, but not many fathers.** A tutor passes on knowledge and leaves when class ends; a father passes on life and walks with you for a lifetime. A tutor asks whether the student understands. A father asks whether the child is thriving, growing up, able to build a home, and one day ready to become a father too.

Many churches today have no shortage of pulpits or programs. What they lack are spiritual parents willing to share their own lives. Jesus' Great Commission is not "make church members of all nations" but "make disciples of all nations": go, baptize, and teach them to obey. That is the whole journey of a parent, from pregnancy and birth through nursing and training until the child has a family of their own.

body.h: Picture this: an orphanage and a home
body.t: An orphanage has beds, meals and classes, but no one who calls you "my child." A home may be simple, yet it has parents who know your name, remember your birthday and get up for you in the night. If the church is only a well-run orphanage, spiritual babies will be undernourished and die young. If the church is a family where everyone has spiritual parents, it will flourish generation after generation.

Spiritual parenthood is not reserved for a few spiritual giants. If you have been born of God, you carry God's life, and life can bring forth life. This handbook walks with the family of the Kingdom, step by step, as we learn to become spiritual parents.

reflect: Since I came to faith, who have been my spiritual parents? What did they do that helped me grow?

intro.title: The Foundation of a Spiritual Parent

verses.text: I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you.
All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness, so that the servant of God may be thoroughly equipped for every good work.
But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak on his own; he will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is yet to come.

body.t: How high a house can rise depends on how deep its foundation goes. A spiritual parent without a foundation will only see a bigger collapse as more people follow. The 321 Principles are the foundation, the pillars and the direction of spiritual parenthood:

head: Principle
What it means for a spiritual parent
rows: I lead people the way Jesus led his disciples: choosing, being with them, teaching, sending, laying down his life.
What I teach is God's Word, not my opinion; my methods must also agree with Scripture.
The Holy Spirit is my guide
Whom to adopt, when to speak, how to walk alongside: I ask the Spirit to lead rather than lean on my own cleverness.
My spiritual children are not my children but God's. I do not rule over them; I help them let Jesus be King.
Let Jesus receive all the glory
When my children grow, the credit is not mine. Everything is what God has done in Jesus.
Generation passing to generation, we establish God's domain on earth, so that the Lord's Prayer is fulfilled: hallowed be your name, your kingdom come.

body.h: Picture this: the pipe and the spring
body.t: A spiritual parent is a pipe, not the spring. The cleaner and clearer the pipe, the more living water reaches the children. When the pipe tries to be the spring, it runs dry, and the children go thirsty.

reflect: Which of the Three Foundations do I neglect most often?
When I lead people, do I sometimes try to become their king without noticing?

intro.title: The Five-Stage Blueprint

verses.text: I am writing to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, dear children, because you know the Father.
And the things you have heard me say in the presence of many witnesses entrust to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others.

body.t: Natural parents follow a clear path: pregnancy, birth, nursing, training, and a home of their own. Spiritual parents do the same. This handbook calls it the **Five Stages**:

items: **Conceive** (pregnancy), which is spiritual adoption: In prayer, receive someone as entrusted to you by God; carry them in love and share the gospel until their heart opens.
**Birth** (delivery): Share the gospel clearly and walk with them as they believe, commit their life and are baptized. New life is born.
**Nurture** (nursing): Shepherd them with God's Word and loving presence until they can feed themselves and walk on their own.
**Train** (raising): Pass on the life of Christ and the 321 Principles by example, by word and by laying down your life.
**Multiply** (a new home): Help them become spiritual parents who raise spiritual grandchildren, generation after generation.

body.t: First John describes three stages of spiritual life: **children**, who know the Father and need to be loved and fed; **young men**, who have overcome the evil one and are strong in God's Word; and **fathers**, who know him who is from the beginning and can raise others (1 John 2:12-14). The Five Stages walk a person from child to father.
The Five Stages are tied closely to the 920 and 235 practices:

items: **920**: Everyone I am in relationship with is my "2." I practice living a selfless "0" life and bear the "9" fruit of the Spirit. The people I adopt are part of my 920.

**235**: With other selfless people I build "2" spiritual companionship, "3" spiritual parent-child relationships, and "5" five-fold ministry teams of spiritual comrades. The Five Stages build the "3" and grow it into the "5."

reflect: Which of the Five Stages are the people around me in right now?
Which stage of 1 John am I in myself?

intro.title: The Life of a Spiritual Parent
intro.tag: Selfless · Life first, then relationships, then ministry

verses.text: I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
He must become greater; I must become less.
But he gives us more grace. That is why Scripture says: "God opposes the proud but shows favor to the humble."

body.t: The greatest enemy of a spiritual parent is not Satan, nor busyness, but a **self-centered** heart: I want to be needed, I want to be thanked, I want my children to listen to me, I want my team to be big. Self-centered parents raise self-centered children. Pride provokes pride, and everyone loses.

Being **selfless** does not mean becoming nothing. It means letting Christ live in me, entering the infinite and living out the infinite. John the Baptist was a selfless spiritual father. He handed his own disciples to Jesus and said, "He must become greater; I must become less."

John called himself the friend of the bridegroom (John 3:29). What makes the best man happiest is seeing the bride given to the groom, not seeing her fall for the best man. A spiritual parent brings children to Jesus so that they fall in love with Jesus, not with me.
The order for a spiritual parent is **life first, then relationships, then ministry**:

items: **Life**: I first walk with God and am fed by him every day. Only then do I have milk to feed others.
**Relationships**: People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things. Never hurt people for the sake of a task, or damage relationships for the sake of progress.
**Ministry**: Reading partnerships, small groups and baptism classes are tools, the fruit of life and relationship, not the goal.

body.t: Relationships also have an order: first my relationship with God, then with myself, then with others, and only then with tasks.

reflect: When I lead people, where does my self-centeredness show up most? (being needed, being thanked, watching numbers...)
Is my relationship with God today full enough that I have "milk" to feed others?

intro.title: How to Use This Handbook

verses.text: Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God's will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.

body.t: Change your mindset and you change your life; change your life and you change how you live. Every chapter follows the **eight steps for changing mindsets**. Please don't just read through it. Walk through it:

items: **Information**: Read the Scripture and the chapter to learn what God says.
**Revelation**: Pray quietly and ask the Holy Spirit to make one sentence come alive in your heart.
**Conviction**: Speak God's perspective aloud with the Declaration of Faith.
**Practice**: Tick the chapter's practices and do them this week.
**Review**: Assess yourself honestly with the Self-Check.
**Correction**: Note what you need to adjust in My Notes.
**Repetition**: Practice each chapter for at least four weeks until it becomes habit.
**Multiplication**: Read this chapter with your own spiritual children.
**On your own**: One chapter a week, completing a round in five weeks. Each time someone new comes into your life, return to the chapter for the stage they are in.
**Spiritual parent and child**: Read a section together each time you meet and share using the small-group questions.
**Small groups**: A five-week cycle. Leaders use the discussion questions, and in the last week everyone makes the declaration together.
**Your spiritual family**: On the Family page, record where each spiritual child is in the Five Stages and pray for them.

body.t: Use your heart and rely on the Spirit, not your head and yourself. Everything you do flows from the heart, and the Spirit lives in your heart, not in your head.

reflect: How long am I willing to take for my first round of the Five Stages?
Whom will I invite to read this handbook with me?

stages.name: Conceive
stages.tag: Conceiving is spiritual adoption · Carrying spiritual children in prayer
stages.oneLine: In prayer, receive someone as entrusted to you by God, and carry them in love until their heart opens.

verses.text: I urge, then, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercession and thanksgiving be made for all people—
He told them, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into his harvest field."
Don't you have a saying, 'It's still four months until harvest'? I tell you, open your eyes and look at the fields! They are ripe for harvest.
And pray for us, too, that God may open a door for our message, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
But in your hearts revere Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give an answer to everyone who asks you to give the reason for the hope that you have. But do this with gentleness and respect,

meaning.t: Conceiving is spiritual adoption. Physical life begins with conception, and spiritual life begins the same way: in prayer I receive the people God has placed around me as entrusted to me, and in love I lead them to Jesus. So whenever this chapter speaks of adoption, it means conceiving spiritual children.

To **adopt** spiritually is first to **acknowledge**: this person is not in my life by accident. God placed them in my 920 and entrusted them to me. Then it is to **lead**: in prayer I bring them before God, and in daily life I bring them toward Jesus.

Conceiving, which is spiritual adoption, is like pregnancy. For nine months a mother cannot see her child, and the child does not know her, yet every meal and every breath she takes nourishes him. Spiritual adoption works the same way. The person does not yet know Jesus and may not even know you are praying, but day by day you carry them in prayer and love. **Without pregnancy there is no birth; without adoption there are no spiritual children.**

meaning.h: Picture this: seeds in a greenhouse
meaning.t: A seed buried in soil shows nothing on the surface. If the farmer digs it up every day to see whether it has sprouted, it will die. The season of adoption calls for patience: watering (prayer), sunlight (love), and waiting for God's time. "Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up" (Galatians 6:9).

mindset: Evangelism is the pastor's job.
Everyone born of God is called to be a spiritual parent.
I'll wait until they're ready.
The fields are ripe for harvest; often the one who is not ready is me.
I'm not a good speaker.
When the Spirit comes we receive power; a selfless life is the most powerful gospel.
Evangelism feels like selling, and I fear rejection.
Evangelism is a relationship of love; I sow and water, and God makes it grow.
If they say no, I've failed.
Obedience is success; I leave the results to God and keep loving and praying.

model.jesus: Before Jesus chose his disciples, he prayed all night: "Jesus went out to a mountainside to pray, and spent the night praying to God. When morning came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also designated apostles" (Luke 6:12-13). Adoption begins on your knees.
model.bible: God "wants all people to be saved and to come to a knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:4). So the people I adopt are not just "people I like" but "people God has placed around me."
model.spirit: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you the "person of peace" (Luke 10:6). The Spirit will place a name, a burden or a chance meeting in your heart. Follow that prompting.

steps.d: Using five circles of life, write down 20 names: family and relatives, coworkers and classmates, neighbors, friends and fellow hobbyists, and people who serve you (shopkeepers, medical staff, drivers...). Each of them is a "2" in your 920.

Be still before God and ask the Spirit to prompt you to circle three to five of the twenty as your adoption list for this season. The number does not need to be large; it needs to be real and sustained.

At a set time each day, pray for each person by name: first, that God will open their heart; second, that God will open a door for the message; third, that God will give me love for them and the right opportunities.
Practice selflessness in this relationship and bear the fruit of the Spirit. Each week, show them one concrete act of love: a message, a meal, a helping hand, a small gift.

Be a friend first, not a preacher. Listen carefully to their family, work, pressures, hopes and pain. Write them down and turn them into prayer. When people feel loved, they become willing to hear about God's love.
At the right time, take three minutes to tell how Jesus changed you: before you believed, how you came to believe, and life since then. Keep it real, brief and focused on Jesus.

Invite them to a small group, a Sunday service, a festival gathering or the Air Fellowship, or to read a passage from the Gospels together. An invitation is sowing; whether they say yes or no, leave it to God.

tools.body: Dear Father, thank you for loving me first and rescuing me out of darkness. Today I adopt ____ before you. I acknowledge that you have placed them in my life. Please open their heart so they see their need for you. Please open a door for the message and prepare the right time and the right words. Take away my self-centeredness, fear and pride, and let Jesus live in me so that they can see Christ in me. I place them in your hands. The results are yours, and all the glory belongs to Jesus. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.

items: Family and relatives: parents, spouse, children, siblings, extended family
Coworkers and classmates: office, school, clubs
Neighbors and community: building, street, parents of your children's classmates
Friends and fellow hobbyists: sports, interests, old friends, online friends
People who serve you: regular shops, medical staff, drivers, repair workers

tools.t: Five Questions That Open Spiritual Conversations
items: What has been putting the most pressure on you lately?
What do you think matters most in life?
When you hit a wall you can't get past, what do you usually do?
Have you ever wondered where people go after they die?
If God is real, what would you most want to ask him?
Before (about 1 minute): my life then and the emptiness or struggle in my heart (be specific; don't exaggerate)
How I believed (about 1 minute): how I heard the gospel and why I was willing to let Jesus be King
After (about 1 minute): how Jesus has changed my mindset, life, daily living and relationships
A closing invitation: "If you'd like, I'd be glad to tell you more about this Jesus."
tools.note: The testimony writer on the Tools page helps you write it step by step and copy it.

qa.q: Family members are the hardest to reach. What should I do?
qa.a: Our families watch our lives more than they listen to our preaching. Start by living selflessly at home: admit your faults, serve, show respect, don't argue. Peter says unbelieving husbands "may be won over without words by the behavior of their wives" (1 Peter 3:1). Pray over the long haul, and ask other brothers and sisters to connect with your family. Sometimes one sentence from an "outsider" does more than ten from you.

qa.q: They are clearly not interested, or even resentful.
qa.a: Stop talking, but don't stop loving. Shift your focus from "getting them to listen" to "letting them be loved." Keep praying, and be the first to show up when they hit trouble. Many people remember "that Christian who was always kind to me" at the lowest point of their lives.

qa.q: How long should I keep someone on my adoption list? What if nothing happens?
qa.a: Adoption has no deadline, because love has no deadline. You can adjust your list in prayer each season, but don't give up on people lightly. If nothing seems to happen, examine yourself: do I really love them, or do I just want to finish a task? God values your faithfulness more than your results.

qa.q: My own life isn't good enough yet. Can I still adopt people?
qa.a: Yes. The man born blind said, "One thing I do know. I was blind but now I see!" (John 9:25). He couldn't yet explain doctrine, but he could already testify. You don't need to be perfect, only real. Along the way, God will renew you too.

stages.name: Birth
stages.oneLine: Share the gospel clearly and walk with them as they believe, commit their life and are baptized: welcome a new life.

verses.text: Jesus replied, "Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again."
Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God—

If you declare with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For it is with your heart that you believe and are justified, and it is with your mouth that you profess your faith and are saved.
Peter replied, "Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit."
We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life.

meaning.t: Paul says, "In Christ Jesus I **became your father through the gospel**." Spiritual birth means bringing people into God's family through the gospel. New birth is the work of the Holy Spirit (John 3:6), but God delights to use spiritual parents as "midwives": sharing the gospel clearly, inviting a response, and walking with someone through their commitment and baptism.

A **commitment to Christ** is like a baby being born: life has begun. **Baptism** is like registering the birth and taking the family name: publicly entering Christ and God's household. Parents need to be present for both.

meaning.h: Picture this: the father outside the delivery room
meaning.t: When a child is born, a father doesn't say, "Good, it's born. I'm off to work." He stays close, holds the baby, notes the time, and celebrates the day every year. Spiritual parents also stay close to new life, record the spiritual birthday, and celebrate and bless it every year.

mindset: I have to convince them.
The Spirit convicts the world of sin, righteousness and judgment (John 16:8); I only need to share clearly and let the Spirit work.
The gospel is a set of doctrines.
The gospel is a living Lord Jesus; it is an invitation to move from "I am king" to "Let Jesus be King."
They committed their life; job done.
Commitment is a birth, not a graduation; nurturing must start right away.
Baptism should wait until they become very good.
Baptism is the beginning of obedient faith, an enrollment, not a graduation; preparation is about understanding and sincerity, not perfection.
Leading someone to faith is my achievement.
People are born of God; I am only the midwife, and all glory goes to Jesus.

model.jesus: At the well Jesus talked with the Samaritan woman (John 4). He moved from water to living water, from her needs to her sin, until she recognized him as the Messiah and went back to town to testify. Jesus began with her need and ended by pointing to himself.
model.bible: Scripture defines the content of the gospel: God's love, human sin, Christ's death and resurrection, and our repentance and faith (1 Corinthians 15:3-4). Nothing added, nothing taken away, no human opinion in its place.
model.spirit: Before sharing, ask to be filled with the Spirit. While sharing, watch for the Spirit at work in the other person: tears in their eyes, a long silence, questions beginning to come. That is harvest time.

steps.d: Before sharing the gospel, confess your sins, pray and ask to be filled with the Spirit. Come with love, not a desire to win. Ask one or two companions to pray during your conversation.
Begin with their struggles, questions or hopes, such as stress, relationships, meaning or death, so they see that the gospel has to do with their life.

Use the Four Gospel Steps: God loves you; we have sinned (the self-centered heart sits on the throne); Jesus died and rose for you; you need to respond by letting Jesus be King. Keep it simple, clear and grounded in Scripture.

Ask gently and clearly, "Would you like to receive Jesus now as the Lord and Savior of your life?" If yes, lead them through the commitment prayer line by line. If not yet, respect that and set a time to talk again.
Use 1 John 5:12-13 to show them that salvation rests on God's promise, not on feelings. Tell them, "From today, you are a child of God." Record their spiritual birthday.

The first two days are when newborns are most fragile. Contact them the very next day, read their first passage together (the Gospel of John is a good start), teach them their first prayer, and introduce them to one or two brothers and sisters.

Use the four baptism preparation lessons to help them understand salvation, baptism, new life and the church family. Help them write their baptism testimony, be there on the day to bless them, and celebrate with their family.

items.vt: "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life."
items.d: God created you and loves you deeply. He wants you to have abundant life.

items.vt: "For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God." "For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord."
items.d: The root of sin is a self-centered heart: leaving our human place, putting ourselves in charge as king, trying to take God's place. The result is separation from God and a life without direction.

items.vt: "But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us."
items.d: Jesus' death dealt with our sinful acts and our sinful nature; his resurrection gives us new life.

items.vt: "Yet to all who did receive him, to those who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God."
items.d: Repent: turn from "I am king" to "Let Jesus be King." Believe: welcome Jesus into your heart.

tools.body: Dear Father, I confess that I am a sinner. I have been running my own life as my own king, and I have turned away from you. Thank you for loving me and sending your Son Jesus to die on the cross for me, bearing my sins. I believe that he rose from the dead on the third day. Lord Jesus, I now open the door of my heart and welcome you into my life as my Savior and my King. Please forgive all my sins and give me new life. Holy Spirit, please live in my heart and guide me to follow you all my life. Thank you that from today I am a child of God. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.

qa.q: They said, "Let me think about it." What now?
qa.a: Respect that and don't pressure them. You might ask, "What is your main concern?" Often there is a specific issue behind it: family, ancestors, a particular sin, or an impression of the church. Set a time to meet again and keep praying. Sometimes the Spirit works in a moment; sometimes it takes ten years.

qa.q: Their family opposes baptism, or worries about ancestor rites.
qa.a: First affirm their desire to honor their parents; Scripture also teaches us to honor father and mother. Explain that Christians remember their ancestors and honor their elders in other ways, such as memorial services and spending more time caring for parents. Pray with your pastors about the timing of baptism, but help them stand firm in faith while winning their family with love and respect.

qa.q: They ask, "Why can't good people go to heaven?"
qa.a: Use an analogy: passing an exam takes 60 points, but God's standard is 100 points of holiness, and no one can reach it however good they are (Romans 3:23). Salvation isn't about our score. Jesus took the test for us, scored 100, and hands us his report card (Ephesians 2:8-9). The question isn't good people versus bad people; it is who sits on the throne.

qa.q: They committed their life, then disappeared.
qa.a: Premature babies need an incubator. Keep in touch, but don't chase them like a debt collector. Send a verse, a greeting, an invitation to a meal. Then review: was the commitment rushed? Was there no 48-hour follow-up? Were they never brought into a spiritual family? With the next new life, follow up sooner and more closely.

stages.name: Nurture
stages.oneLine: Shepherd them with God's Word and loving presence until they can feed themselves and walk on their own.

verses.text: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation,

Instead, we were like young children among you. Just as a nursing mother cares for her children, so we cared for you. Because we loved you so much, we were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God but our lives as well.
When they had finished eating, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?" "Yes, Lord," he said, "you know that I love you." Jesus said, "Feed my lambs."

Be shepherds of God's flock that is under your care, watching over them—not because you must, but because you are willing, as God wants you to be; not pursuing dishonest gain, but eager to serve; not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.

And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

meaning.t: A newborn cannot find milk on its own, cannot roll over and certainly cannot protect itself. It needs someone to feed it on schedule, hold it often and watch over it carefully. Spiritual nurture means **feeding with God's Word, holding with loving presence and surrounding with the protection of prayer**, until they can read the Bible and pray on their own (feeding themselves) and gather and serve on their own (walking).
Jesus asked Peter, "Do you love me? Feed my lambs." The motivation for nurture is not duty but love for the Lord. Those who love the Lord love the lambs he loves.

Whatever a mother eats ends up in her milk. If spiritual parents are filled with God's Word every day, what they give is "pure spiritual milk." If they are dry, all they have left to give is rules and fatigue. So nurturing others begins with your own morning time with God.

mindset: Once they are in church, the pastor takes over.
Whoever gives birth must also nurture; no parent leaves a newborn at the hospital door.
Nurture means helping them take classes.
Nurture means sharing life: eating together, praying together, facing hardship together.
They should grow up on their own.
Babies need milk; an unfed baby does not grow up. It dies.
If they depend on me, I am doing well.
I want them to depend on Jesus, not on me; selfless parents help their children fall in love with the Father.
Their weakness is their own problem.
The weak need more support: "We who are strong ought to bear with the failings of the weak" (Romans 15:1).

model.jesus: After his resurrection, Jesus prepared a fire on the shore with fish and bread for his tired disciples and said, "Come and have breakfast" (John 21:12). He fed Peter's stomach first, then healed his heart, and only then entrusted him with his mission: life first, then relationship, then ministry.
model.bible: Scripture is both milk and solid food (Hebrews 5:12-14). What we feed people is God's Word, not our own stories. Experience can be shared, but only truth truly nourishes.
model.spirit: Before each meeting, pray, "Holy Spirit, what do they most need today?" Sometimes it is a verse, sometimes a meal, sometimes simply, "I'm here with you."

steps.d: In the first month, meet face to face at least once a week and send a short greeting every day. After that, meet weekly and check in every two or three days. Consistency matters more than intensity.
Use the Eight-Week New Believer Reading Plan: one theme, one passage and one practice each week. Pray together after reading, and review it the next week.
Teach them to pray with the Lord's Prayer and to read Scripture every day with Morning Reading 321, starting with ten minutes a day. You model it first, then invite them to lead.

steps.t: Bring them into a spiritual family
steps.d: Bring them into a small group, Sunday worship and the Air Fellowship, and help them get to know at least three brothers and sisters. One spiritual parent is not enough; they need a whole family.
New believers often face spiritual battles: family opposition, old habits, doubts and temptation. Form a small prayer network and teach them to put on the full armor of God (Ephesians 6:10-18).
When they fall, listen first, then open Scripture, and finally bring it to Jesus together to confess and receive forgiveness. Don't scold, don't give up and don't cover it up.
Help them see that the people around them are their "2." Starting at home, they practice selflessness and bear the fruit of the Spirit. Step by step they move from being nurtured to nurturing others.

qa.a: Asking a baby to run before it can walk is unreasonable. First let them be sure they are loved and accepted, then speak the truth in love at the right time. When correcting, deal with the issue rather than attacking the person, and look together to Jesus for forgiveness and power.

qa.a: Fit nurture into the rhythm you already have: lunch together, school runs together, a call on the way to work, checking in together on Morning Reading 321. stages.name: Train
stages.tag: By example · By word · By life
stages.oneLine: Pass on the life of Christ and the 321 Principles by example, by word and by laying down your life.

verses.text: Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ.
Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me—put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you.

These commandments that I give you today are to be on your hearts. Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Very truly I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds.
For you know that we dealt with each of you as a father deals with his own children, encouraging, comforting and urging you to live lives worthy of God, who calls you into his kingdom and glory.

meaning.t: Nurture keeps a child alive; training helps a child grow up. Spiritual training is not running a course. It is **life shaping life**. Paul says, "Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me." Those four verbs cover three kinds of training:

items.p: Live it so they can see
Explain it so they can hear

meaning.t: With only **words**, children can talk but not do. With **example** but no words, they see but don't understand why. Without **laying down your life**, everything else is just technique. Laying down your life is being the kernel of wheat that falls to the ground and dies: paying the price of time, money, emotional energy and reputation, even your own comfort and rights. Paul says, "We were delighted to share with you not only the gospel of God but our lives as well." That is training by life.

meaning.h: Picture this: learning to ride a bike
meaning.t: No one learns to ride after one lecture on the principles of cycling. A father rides first so the child can see (example). He explains: look ahead and keep pedaling (word). Then he holds the back of the seat and runs alongside until he is out of breath with a scraped knee (life). Finally, without the child noticing, he gently lets go.

mindset: Training means lecturing and classes.
Training means passing on life; courses are tools, life is the content.
I must be perfect before I can teach.
I walk with them on the road of following Christ; even how I confess and repent is an example.
They should listen to me.
They should listen to Jesus; I teach them to hear God for themselves through Scripture and the Spirit.
The more I teach, the better.
Teach one thing, do one thing, complete one thing; changing mindsets means walking all eight steps.
I've given so much; they should be grateful.
Laying down your life seeks no return; when a kernel of wheat dies, it is dead, and the fruit belongs to God.

model.jesus: Jesus "appointed twelve that they might be with him and that he might send them out to preach" (Mark 3:14). Being with them was example, his teaching was word, the cross was life. Jesus washed his disciples' feet and then said, "I have set you an example."
model.bible: Scripture is both the material and the standard for training (2 Timothy 3:16-17): teaching (what is right), rebuking (what is wrong), correcting (how to return to what is right) and training in righteousness (how to keep walking in it).
model.spirit: The true teacher is the Holy Spirit (John 14:26). After teaching, spiritual parents hand their children over to the Spirit: "Holy Spirit, please plant today's words in their heart."

steps.t: Be with them: let them into your life
steps.d: Invite them to eat with you, visit people with you, serve with you, even do household chores with you. What they see beside you outweighs what they hear from you.

steps.t: Model it: the Five-Step Coaching Method
steps.d: I do, you watch → I do, you help → you do, I help → you do, I watch → you do, others watch. Use it for prayer, leading Bible study, visiting, sharing the gospel and every other ministry.

steps.t: Teach: pass on the 321 Principles systematically
steps.d: Teach the Three Foundations, the Two Cores and the One Purpose in order, along with self-centered versus selfless, humility versus pride, and life first, then relationships, then ministry. Pair every idea with Scripture.

steps.t: Practice: one assignment at a time
steps.d: Give one concrete practice each week. At the next meeting, review it first: What did you do? What happened? What did you learn? What needs to change?

steps.t: Correct: speak the truth in love
steps.d: When you see a problem, say so, but privately, in love, addressing the issue rather than the person, and return together to Scripture (Ephesians 4:15). After correcting, affirm and accept them.

steps.t: Lay down your life: pay a price for them
steps.d: Show up when they need you most: the midnight call, the hospital visit, financial help, standing with them when they are misunderstood. This is not heroism; it is taking up your cross every day.

steps.t: Release: let them begin to serve
steps.d: Watch for their gifts and burdens, refer to the five-fold ministry (Ephesians 4:11), and let them start with small tasks, with room to make mistakes and plenty of encouragement.

qa.q: They made a mistake. How do I correct them without hurting the relationship?
qa.a: Pray first and make sure your motive is love, not anger. Talk privately (Matthew 18:15). Affirm them first, then name the facts and the biblical standard specifically, and finally look for a way forward together and pray for them. Afterward, let your actions say, "I am still your spiritual parent. I haven't gone anywhere."

qa.q: They know the Bible better than I do. Can I still train them?
qa.a: Spiritual parenthood is not about who knows more, but about who is more willing to lay down self. You can learn knowledge from them; they can learn life from you. Humility inspires humility, and everyone wins.

qa.q: I failed, and they saw it. What now?
qa.a: This is one of the most valuable moments to teach by example. Be honest with them, confess to God, and apologize to people where needed. Let them see that Christians are not people who never fall, but people who know how to return to the cross when they do. Pride is what would lose them; humility will win them.

qa.q: How do I know they have grown up?
qa.a: Look at fruit, not years: they are fed by God's Word on their own; they pray first when trouble comes; they live out 920 at home and at work; they can share the gospel clearly; they begin to care for and lead others. When they start asking, "How do I lead someone?", they are ready for the Multiply stage.

stages.name: Multiply
stages.oneLine: Help your spiritual children become spiritual parents who raise spiritual grandchildren, generation after generation.

verses.text: And the things you have heard me say in the presence of many witnesses entrust to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples.

God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground."
So Christ himself gave the apostles, the prophets, the evangelists, the pastors and teachers, to equip his people for works of service, so that the body of Christ may be built up

meaning.t: Fruit is not meant to hang on the tree looking nice. It carries seeds that can grow into another tree. **Multiplication** means helping your spiritual children become spiritual parents who raise spiritual grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Second Timothy 2:2 spans four generations: **Paul → Timothy → reliable people → others**.

A spiritual parent is not measured by how many people surround them, but by **whether they have spiritual grandchildren**. Children without grandchildren is addition; children who have children is multiplication.

Suppose every spiritual parent leads one person to faith each year and trains that person to become a spiritual parent too. After year 1 there are 2 people, after year 5 there are 32, after year 10 there are 1,024, after year 20 more than a million, and after year 30 more than a billion. The Great Commission is not completed by a few stars but by generation after generation of spiritual parents.

Multiplication also builds **235**: from the "3" of spiritual parent and child, you grow together into "2" spiritual companions, and finally stand side by side as a "5" five-fold ministry team. This is how we build a God-centered system on earth, so that "your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven" is fulfilled.

mindset: The more people I lead, the better.
Success is when those I lead can lead others; look at grandchildren, not just children.
They are my people, my team.
They are God's children; I am only a steward. Let Jesus be King and let Jesus receive the glory.
If I let go, I will lose them.
Letting go is how multiplication happens; a clenched fist cannot raise the next generation.
They aren't good enough yet; let's wait.
Timothy was entrusted while young; faithfulness matters more than perfection, and people grow by serving.
If they surpass me, I'll feel lost.
He must become greater; I must become less. Children surpassing their parents is a parent's greatest joy.

model.jesus: Jesus had only three years on earth, yet he entrusted his mission to eleven ordinary disciples, saying, "As the Father has sent me, I am sending you" (John 20:21). Then he ascended and handed the stage to them and to the Holy Spirit. Jesus is the spiritual father who knew best how to let go.
model.bible: From the beginning God blessed humanity to "be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth" (Genesis 1:28), and the Great Commission is to "make disciples of all nations." Multiplication is God's heart, not a church-growth strategy.
model.spirit: After Pentecost, the church spread as the Spirit led: Philip, Peter, Barnabas, Paul, one bringing the next. Ask the Holy Spirit: among my children, who are the "reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others"?

steps.t: Share the vision from day one
steps.d: From the day they come to faith, tell them, "One day you will be a spiritual parent too." Let them know they are being nurtured so that they can nurture others.
Draw their relationship map together, circle their adoption list and pray for it with them. Spiritual grandparents pray for their grandchildren too.
Go out together: first you speak and they listen, then they speak and you fill in, and finally they speak on their own while you pray nearby.
Once they begin reading with someone, check in every two weeks: "How are your spiritual children? What difficulties are you facing?" Be their advisor without taking their place.
When they can lead people on their own, affirm and empower them publicly. Let them become the primary spiritual parent while you step back as a spiritual grandparent who keeps praying and blessing.

Move with them from the "3" of parent and child to the "2" of spiritual companions who hold each other accountable. Then together invite other selfless people to form a "5" five-fold ministry team of spiritual comrades.
Hold regular spiritual family gatherings to count God's grace, lay hands on and send out new spiritual parents, give thanks in everything, and give all the glory to Jesus.

tools.body: I, ____, born of God by his grace, today commit myself before God and before everyone: Jesus is my model, Scripture is my standard, and the Holy Spirit is my guide. I will let Jesus be King in me, and let Jesus receive all the glory. I will conceive, birth, nurture, train and multiply the spiritual children God entrusts to me, loving them to the end by example, by word and by laying down my life, without controlling them, taking credit or giving up on them. With the family of the Kingdom I will build a God-centered system until the Lord Jesus returns. Amen.

items: Worship (15 minutes)
Counting grace: one testimony from each generation (20 minutes)
Scripture: 2 Timothy 2:2 or 3 John 1:4 (15 minutes)

qa.q: They don't want to lead anyone; they only want to be fed.
qa.a: First check whether the vision was never made clear, or whether they are still at the "children" stage. Keep sharing the vision, and let them join your adoption and evangelism, starting by "watching from the side." Many people aren't unwilling, just afraid. Presence and modeling bring courage.

qa.q: What if they eventually surpass me and have more influence?
qa.a: Praise God! This is a spiritual parent's greatest joy (3 John 1:4). John the Baptist said, "He must become greater; I must become less." If you feel a sense of loss, that is God shining light on your self-centeredness. Confess it, then go and bless them.

qa.q: They left for another church or ministry.
qa.a: They are God's child, not my property. If it is God's leading, bless and send them. If there was hurt, do all you can to restore the relationship. The Kingdom is bigger than any local church, and Jesus being King matters more than our team.

qa.q: How do I avoid becoming a controlling spiritual parent?
qa.a: Ask yourself three questions: Do I want them to report everything to me? Do I care whether they are "my people"? When they make decisions, do they ask God first or me first? A spiritual parent's authority is the authority to serve, not to lord it over others (1 Peter 5:3). Invite your spiritual companions to examine you regularly.

appendix.title: Glossary
terms: Three Foundations (Jesus is my model, Scripture is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide), Two Cores (let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory), One Purpose (build a God-centered system).
Self-centered is the old life that revolves around me and sits on the throne trying to take God's place; selfless is the new life in which it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me.
Everyone in relationship with me is my "2"; I practice living a selfless "0" life and bear the "9" fruit of the Spirit.
"2" spiritual companionship, "3" spiritual parent-child relationships, "5" five-fold ministry teams of spiritual comrades.
Conceive, Birth, Nurture, Train and Multiply: the five stages in which a spiritual parent walks with someone from unbelief to becoming a spiritual parent.
By example (living it), by word (explaining it), by life (laying down your life in love).
Receiving in prayer the people God has placed in my life as entrusted to me, and praying for and caring for them until they come to faith.
The day someone commits their life to Christ and is born of God.
Luke 10:6: someone God has prepared who is ready to welcome the gospel.
The process of changing mindsets: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition, multiplication.

role.title: The Leader's Role
paras: A small group leader is not a preacher or a teacher but a spiritual parent. Your task is not to get through the material, but to walk with each member through the eight steps for changing mindsets: information, revelation, conviction, practice, review, correction, repetition and multiplication.

The best small group is the one where the leader says the least and the Holy Spirit does the most. The better you prepare, the more you can let go in the room; the more selfless you are, the more easily your members meet Jesus.

Remember: life first, then relationships, then ministry. More important than covering the material is that everyone is seen, heard and prayed for. Never hurt people for the sake of a task, or damage relationships for the sake of progress.

Adoption covers "people God has placed around me," not just "people I like."

activity.d: Give everyone a sheet of paper. Draw five concentric circles (family, coworkers and classmates, neighbors, friends, people who serve you) and write in twenty names. After three minutes of silent prayer, circle three to five. Share in pairs and pray for each other's lists.

tips: Someone may say, "I don't know any unbelievers." Gently guide them to start with the "people who serve you" circle.
Don't let sharing turn into criticizing family members; the focus is "how I love them," not "what's wrong with them."

shengyu.goal: Help every member share the Four Gospel Steps clearly within ten minutes and lead someone in a commitment prayer.
keys: At its core the gospel is about who is King: moving from "I am king" to "Let Jesus be King."
Commitment is a birth, not a graduation; follow-up within 48 hours decides whether new life survives.
Baptism is an enrollment, not a graduation.

activity.d: In pairs, one plays a seeker while the other shares the Four Gospel Steps in eight minutes; then swap. Finally, share as a group: Which step was hardest? What is a seeker most likely to ask?

tips: Ask those playing seekers not to be deliberately difficult; build confidence first.
Remind members that mistakes are fine; the Spirit uses people willing to open their mouths.

yangyu.goal: Help every member learn the five mentoring questions and the eight-week plan, and commit to walking with one new believer.
keys: Whoever gives birth must nurture; nurture is sharing life, not just classes.
Spiritual parents must be fed first so that what they give is pure spiritual milk.
The goal is for them to love and depend on Jesus, not to be unable to live without me.

activity.d: In threes: one asks the five mentoring questions, one answers and one observes and gives feedback. Six minutes per round; rotate three times. Observers notice: did the questioner listen all the way?

tips: If a member is a new believer themselves, pair them with a mature brother or sister.
Remind everyone that mentoring conversations are confidential.

jiaoyu.goal: Help every member understand training by example, word and life, and begin coaching someone with the five-step method.
keys: Words make people understand, example makes people believe, self-giving makes people change.
I don't need to be perfect to train others; even how I confess and repent is an example.
Five-step coaching: I do, you watch; I do, you help; you do, I help; you do, I watch; you do, others watch.

activity.d: Give everyone ten minutes to fill in the matrix (with God, self, others, tasks × by example, word, life). Circle the strongest and weakest cells, then share in pairs and pray for each other.

tips: This chapter can stir up self-blame; keep the focus on God's grace and the next step, not past failures.
As the leader, share your own weakest cell first as an example of humility.

yanyu.goal: Help every member receive the vision of "look at grandchildren, not just children" and make the spiritual parent commissioning covenant before God.
keys: 2 Timothy 2:2 spans four generations: Paul, Timothy, reliable people, others.
Children alone is addition; children who have children is multiplication.
Letting go is how multiplication happens; children surpassing their parents is a parent's greatest joy.

activity.d: Everyone draws their spiritual family tree: their own spiritual parents above, their spiritual children and grandchildren below (including people they are adopting). After sharing, read the commissioning covenant aloud together and bless one another with the laying on of hands.

tips: For members whose tree is still empty: their adoption list is the first generation of their family tree.
Consider a love feast in the final week to celebrate like a family.

course.title: Eight-Week New Believer Course
course.sub: Walk one-on-one with a new believer and lay a firm foundation in eight weeks
intro: A new believer is like a newborn. What they need most is not a pile of information but a spiritual parent willing to walk with them for a while. This course turns "Nurture" into eight concrete meetings: once a week, in person or online, you read Scripture, share, practice and pray together.

The focus is not how well we teach but helping them know Jesus personally: Jesus is their model, Scripture is their standard, and the Holy Spirit is their guide. We simply walk alongside, bringing them to Jesus so that Jesus reigns in them.

By the end of eight weeks they will be assured of salvation, praying, reading the Bible, experiencing the Spirit, overcoming temptation, belonging to God's family, living a selfless new life, and beginning to share their story with their own adoption list. Spiritual children grow up to become spiritual parents.
flow: Listen to their week; open with the five mentoring questions.
Take turns reading this week's passage and say what it means in your own words.
Share the three key points briefly, with everyday examples.
Use the discussion questions and agree on this week's practice.
Invite them to pray in their own words, then bless them.
rules: Life first, then relationships, then ministry: draw near to God daily before you lead others.
Relationship matters more than pace: slow down when needed, even taking a lesson twice.
Keep the focus on Jesus: help them depend on Jesus, not on you.
Listen more, talk less: ask questions and let Scripture and the Spirit speak.
Send one message a week between meetings, a verse or a greeting, so they know someone remembers them.
course.done: When the eight weeks are complete, invite them to be baptized (if they have not been), join a small group regularly, and begin praying for their own adoption list. On the Family page you can move them to the Train stage and keep walking with them by example, by word and by life until they become spiritual parents.

weeks.goal: Help them know for certain that whoever believes in Jesus has eternal life now, resting on God's promise rather than on feelings.
weeks.open: Do you remember receiving a gift you really wanted as a child? How did it feel when you got it?
msg: Eternal life is a gift
1 John says God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. Eternal life is not a certificate we earn but a gift God gives freely. Reach out and receive it, and it is yours.
Whoever has the Son has life
The key is not how you feel today but whether you have received Jesus. John 1:12 says that to all who received Him, who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God.
Assurance comes from God's word
Feelings change like the weather; God's promise stands like a mountain. When doubt comes, open your Bible to these verses and say, "God has said it, and I believe it."
ask: When and how did you decide to receive Jesus?
If someone asked, "Are you sure you are saved?" what would you say?
When are you most likely to doubt your faith?
How does knowing you already have eternal life change the way you face tomorrow?
do: Read 1 John 5:12 aloud every morning
Write the memory verse on a card or your phone wallpaper
Each night, thank God for eternal life in one sentence
Write down the date you came to faith: your spiritual birthday
Tell a Christian friend, "I am a child of God now."
weeks.pray: Dear Father, thank You for sending Jesus to die and rise again for me. I have received Jesus as my Savior and the Lord of my life, and I believe Your word: whoever has the Son has life. From today I will not rely on my feelings but on Your promise that I am Your child and I have eternal life. Holy Spirit, remind me of this every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Listen to the story of their decision first and affirm the step they took.
If they have not yet committed, share the Four Gospel Steps clearly again. Do not rush.
Send a message this week: "You are a child of God. It is true."
weeks.next: Learning to pray: talking with the Father like a child.

I have written these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.
But to all who did receive Him, to those who believed in His name, He gave the right to become children of God—

mem.text: Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.

weeks.goal: Help them understand prayer as a child talking with the Father, and begin praying daily using the Lord's Prayer.
weeks.open: What do you usually talk about with your family or close friends?
msg: Prayer is a child talking with the Father
Jesus taught us to begin with "Our Father in heaven." Prayer does not need fancy words. It is as sincere and natural as a child talking with their dad.
The Lord's Prayer gives prayer a shape
First honor God (hallowed be Your name), then ask for His will to be done, and then pray for daily needs, forgiveness and protection. In this order, our focus stays on God, not on ourselves.
You can pray about everything

Paul says not to be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, to present our requests to God. Big or small, tell God, and His peace that surpasses understanding will guard your heart.
ask: Have you prayed before? How did you pray then?
Which line of the Lord's Prayer touches you most? Why?
What is worrying you most right now?
When and where would you like to pray each day?
do: Pray for five minutes each morning following the Lord's Prayer
Start a prayer notebook and write down requests
Write down one worry and hand it to God
Before bed, name three things you are thankful for
Set a time to pray together with your mentor
weeks.pray: Father, thank You that I can call You "Abba, Father." I want to come and talk with You every day. I hand You every worry in my heart; let Your peace guard my heart and mind. Teach me to pray according to Your will, so that Your name is honored and Your kingdom comes in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Model a simple prayer so they see that prayer can be ordinary.
Pray the Lord's Prayer line by line with them.
Do not correct their words; encourage them to speak.
weeks.next: Daily Bible reading: drawing strength from Scripture every day.

verses.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

mem.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.

weeks.goal: Help them build a daily Bible reading habit, knowing Scripture is God's word and the standard for life.
weeks.open: Have you ever been lost in an unfamiliar place? What did you need most?
msg: Scripture is God-breathed
"All Scripture is God-breathed": God Himself gave His word through human writers. So reading the Bible is listening to God speak to me.
Scripture is the standard for life
Scripture is useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness. It is like a mirror that shows me myself and a ruler that shows me right and wrong.
A lamp to my feet
"Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." A lamp lights the next step, not the whole road of life. Read a little each day and you will have light for today.
ask: What was your impression of the Bible before?
What time of day works best for you to read?
When you come across something you do not understand, what can you do?
Has any verse helped you recently?
do: Read one chapter of John each day (21 chapters)
Write down the sentence that touches you most in each chapter
Reflect with three questions: What do I see? What does it mean? What will I do?
Read the memory verse to a family member or friend
Highlight a sentence in this app and write your reflection
weeks.pray: Lord, thank You for giving me Your word. Open my eyes to see wonderful things in it. I want to read Your word every day and let it be a lamp to my feet and a light to my path. Holy Spirit, help me not only to read but to do what it says. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Look through the Bible's contents with them and help them find John.
Read John 1 together and model the three reflection questions.
Ask each week how far they have read and share what you are learning.
weeks.next: The presence of the Holy Spirit: God lives in us.

verses.text: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

mem.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

weeks.t: The Presence of the Holy Spirit
weeks.goal: Help them know the Holy Spirit as the Helper who lives in believers, and learn to follow His leading and bear His fruit.
weeks.open: Is there someone in your life who often walks with you and helps you?
msg: The Spirit is another Advocate
Jesus promised to ask the Father to give us another Advocate to be with us forever: someone beside you who helps, comforts and guides you.
The Spirit lives in you
"He abides with you and will be in you." You do not face life alone; God Himself lives in your heart. Rely on the Spirit with your heart, not only on yourself with your head.
The fruit of the Spirit
Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. These are not squeezed out by effort; they grow naturally as the Spirit reigns within.
ask: Have you ever sensed God helping or prompting you?
Which of the nine fruits do you need most?
When are you most likely to rely on yourself and forget the Spirit?
Which fruit would you like to grow at home or at work this week?
do: Pray each morning: "Holy Spirit, fill me and guide me."
Choose one fruit a day and look for a chance to live it
Each evening, review where you followed the Spirit and where you did not
Memorize Galatians 5:22-23
Share one experience of the Spirit's help with your mentor
weeks.pray: Holy Spirit, thank You for living in me as my Helper. I give You my heart every day and will no longer rely only on myself. Fill me and guide me, and grow in me love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control, so that others see Jesus in me. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Speak simply about the Spirit, without making them fearful or overly curious.
Share a real example of the Spirit prompting you.
Help them choose one fruit to focus on this week.
weeks.next: Overcoming temptation: God provides a way out.

verses.text: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

mem.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

weeks.goal: Help them know that being tempted is not sin, God always provides a way out, and if they fall they can confess and stand again.
weeks.open: What temptation is hardest for you to resist in daily life right now? (No need to share details.)
msg: Everyone faces temptation
No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. Being tempted does not mean your faith is weak; Jesus Himself was tempted. What matters is how we respond.
God provides a way out

God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear, and with the temptation He will provide a way out. The way out is often to leave the scene, call a spiritual companion, or start praying.
If you fall, confess
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us. Do not hide. Come back to God and back to your spiritual family. Humble confession leads to victory again.
ask: When you faced temptation before, how did you usually handle it?
At what times or in what situations do you fall most easily?
What "way out" can you prepare for yourself?
Who could be your prayer partner in this area?
do: Write down one temptation you often face and ask your spiritual parent to pray
Prepare a specific way out for that temptation
Memorize 1 Corinthians 10:13 this week
When temptation comes, say right away: "Jesus, help me."
If you fall, confess to God that same day and tell your mentor
weeks.pray: Father, thank You that You are faithful and You know my weakness. When temptation comes, remind me to take the way out You provide. I admit that on my own I will fall, but with You I can stand. If I fall, I will come back to You and confess right away, because You will forgive me. Keep me humble and dependent on You, overcoming day by day. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Share your own story of overcoming temptation first to create safety.
Do not press for details; respect what they are ready to share.
Agree on a way to ask for help, such as a simple code message.
weeks.next: God's family: we need one another.

verses.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

mem.text: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.

weeks.goal: Help them understand that faith brings them into God's family, where they need to gather regularly, join a small group, and love one another.
weeks.open: What do you think matters most in a good family?
msg: Faith brings you into God's family
God is our Father, and believers are brothers and sisters. The church is not a building but the family of God.
Do not stop meeting together
Hebrews says not to neglect meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but to encourage one another. A single coal soon goes cold; coals together keep burning.
Spur one another on
The early church devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer. In a small group we read, share and pray together and carry one another.
ask: What was your first impression of church?
What is your biggest obstacle to gathering regularly?
What do you hope to receive in a small group? What can you give?
Which brother or sister would you like to get to know this week?
do: Attend one Sunday service
Attend one small group, in person or online
Get to know three brothers or sisters and write down their names
Pray for one person in your small group
Send an encouraging message to a brother or sister
weeks.pray: Father, thank You for making me part of Your family. I will keep gathering with Your people. Help me open up in my small group and learn to love and support others. Let us spur one another on toward love and good deeds. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Go with them to a service or small group this week.
Introduce them to two or three suitable brothers and sisters.
Watch whether they are being left out in the group.
weeks.next: A selfless new life: no longer I, but Christ.

verses.text: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds. Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.

mem.text: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds. Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

weeks.goal: Help them understand that they are a new creation, and learn to deny themselves so that Jesus lives and reigns in them.
weeks.open: If you could start one thing over, what would it be?
msg: You are a new creation
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away, the new has come. This is not self-improvement; God gives you a completely new life.
No longer I, but Christ
Paul says, "I no longer live, but Christ lives in me." The old self puts itself at the center and wants to be in charge; the new self lets Jesus be King and live within.
Humility overcomes pride

A self-centered person easily becomes proud, comparing and angry; a selfless person returns to their proper place and lets God be God. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your daily living changes. Change starts with me, and at home.
ask: What changes have you noticed in yourself since believing?
In what areas do you most want to be in charge yourself?
What would "letting Jesus be King" look like in your home?
What selfless act of service could you do for your family this week?
do: Memorize Galatians 2:20
Do one act of service at home without expecting anything back
When things go wrong, pause and pray: "Jesus, You are King."
Say sorry or thank you to someone you have been proud toward
Write down three changes from before and after you believed
weeks.pray: Lord Jesus, thank You for making me a new creation. I give You the throne of my life and will no longer be in charge myself. I no longer live, but You live in me. Take away my pride and make me humble and selfless, so that at home and at work people see You. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Share your own struggles in learning selflessness; do not preach.
Help them find one concrete, doable act of service.
Affirm the changes they already show, however small.
weeks.next: Sharing your story: passing on the good news.

verses.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

mem.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.

weeks.goal: Help them write a three-minute testimony, list their own adoption list, and begin to become a spiritual parent to others.
weeks.open: Is there any good news lately that you could not wait to tell someone?
msg: The Spirit gives power to witness
Jesus said we will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on us, and we will be His witnesses. Witnessing depends not on eloquence but on the Spirit's power.
A testimony tells what God has done for you
No arguing needed. Simply share honestly: who you were before, how you met Jesus, and how He has changed you. That is your three-minute testimony.
Answer with gentleness and respect
Peter tells us to always be ready to give an answer, with gentleness and respect. Start with those around you: family, coworkers, friends. They are the people God has placed in your 920.
ask: What was your life like before you believed?
In which area has Jesus changed you most?
Who are three to five people around you that you most want to know Jesus?
How can you start praying for them and caring for them?
do: Write your testimony with the Three-Minute Testimony Writer
Tell your testimony to your mentor once
List three to five names and add them on the Family page
Pray for your adoption list by name every day
Look for a chance to share your testimony with one of them
weeks.pray: Father, thank You for saving me and changing me. Holy Spirit, come upon me and give me power to be Your witness. I place my adoption list in Your hands: open their hearts, open a door for the message, and give me love for them. Let me also become a spiritual parent to others, passing it on from generation to generation. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, Amen.
tip: Have them tell their testimony once and give specific encouragement.
Help them write their adoption list and pray over it together.
Hold a small completion blessing and invite them into the next stage.
weeks.next: Completion: baptism, a regular small group, and beginning to be a spiritual parent.
